neighbours.label: doing something in successive parts: 'in stages / in installments / serial(ised)'
fire: The new bridge will be opened in three stages over the next decade.
Customers can pay for the sofa in monthly installments.
Dickens's novel was first published in serial form in a weekly magazine.
The debt will be repaid in instalments until 2030.
The building was demolished in phases to keep the street open.
The story was serialised in a newspaper before it became a book.
The company plans to roll out the update in several stages.
The museum was renovated in stages while it stayed open.
quiet: The new bridge will be opened in a ceremony next spring.
Customers can pay for the sofa in cash at the counter.
Dickens's novel was first published in hardback by a London firm.
The debt will be repaid in full by the end of 2030.
The building was demolished in a single morning last week.
The story was printed in a newspaper and drew many letters.
The company plans to launch the update in early October.
The museum was renovated in a modern style by the architects.

notes: Card top: stages, serial, installment(s), etapas; logit effect promotes serial, sequential, gradually, progressive. Near misses keep the frame but replace the piecewise manner with an all-at-once or unrelated one.
